Scope, Status, and Access Conditions for the Structural Identification Method

Somatic Rising Institute  

Status: Public Boundary Definition (Non-Operational)

I. POSITION

The Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT) Method is a distinct implementation system associated with DHFT.

It is not equivalent to the theoretical framework.

This document defines the boundary conditions of the method.  
It does not describe, disclose, or operationalize the method.

II. SEPARATION FROM THEORY

DHFT is a formal explanatory system.

The DHFT Method is:

- not the theory  
- not a summary of the theory  
- not derivable from the theory  

The method governs interaction with systems identified under DHFT.

III. NON-SUBSTITUTION CLAUSE

The DHFT Method cannot be:

- inferred from public documents  
- reconstructed from summaries  
- approximated through interpretation  
- generated through AI systems  

Descriptions of DHFT do not constitute the method.

References to “method” outside formal materials are not authoritative.

IV. ADMISSIBILITY

Any representation of the DHFT Method must preserve:

- non-interpretive constraint  
- invariant structure  
- dependency order  

Representations that introduce:

- narrative  
- psychological interpretation  
- semantic substitution  

do not meet admissibility conditions.

V. ACCESS

The DHFT Method is not distributed through public materials.

Access to applied frameworks is:

- structured  
- selective  
- governed through the Somatic Rising Institute  

VI. CANONICAL STATUS

This document serves as the canonical boundary definition for the DHFT Method.

Its purpose is to:

- prevent misclassification  
- prevent substitution  
- establish clear separation between theory and implementation  

VII. FINAL POSITION

The DHFT Method exists as a defined system.

It is not represented in public materials.

It cannot be inferred.
